item.title: You Don't Need a Build System
item.author: raphaeltannous@proton.me (Raphael Tannous)
item.description:
I’ve deployed my website and the digital garden to Cloudflare pages and things are going great. However, the CI/CD pipeline was a mess until I settled on a simple system that just works.

At first, I tried to use Github Actions to build the Hugo site and deploy it, but it had its quirks. Then, I tried to used Cloudflare’s automatic build system, but it was messy.

I asked myself: “Why do we need a remote build system for a frontend site?”

I am already building the Hugo site locally, to review the changes that I am making. Why do I need to wait minutes for Github Actions or Cloudflare to create a container, set up the environment, and build the site?

The public directory already contains the files that need to be published, so I had an idea to create a repository in it, but can I?

YES!

If you are building a Hugo site, and have a .gitignore file, you’ve probably have public in it. The question now is, can I create a repository inside another repository, if that repository ignores the repository that I am about to create?

YES!

The build system is now simple:

  1. Build the Hugo site locally.
  2. Change directory to public.
  3. Push changes.

Now Cloudflare will just have to clone the repo and publish it (it takes seconds).

Keep your pipeline simple :)

Bye-Bye!
